items.title: Build ModruleSync v1 -- standalone static tool (separate repo, not this app)
items.why: Spec, mockup, name, and dedicated repo are all done -- design/SPEC-pgpatcher-priority-merge-tool.md, design/mockup-pgpatcher-priority-merge-tool.html, and github.com/awesmdiver/modrule-sync (local copy at skyrim-modding/modrule-sync, currently just a README). This is the real build pass.
items.prompt:
Build ModruleSync v1 as a standalone, zero-backend static web page, in THIS repo (already
git-initialized, remote origin -> github.com/awesmdiver/modrule-sync, two commits so far: a README
and a CLAUDE.md). Do NOT rewrite this repo's existing README copy -- if the build changes what it
should say, flag that in the handoff for the design side to update (same file-ownership split as
every project in this workspace: terminal doesn't edit README voice).

Read these two files FIRST, in full, before writing any code:
1. `vortex-tools/vortex-collection-tools/design/SPEC-pgpatcher-priority-merge-tool.md` -- the full
   spec: matching algorithm tiers, the canonical-name rule, what gets merged, the UI flow, why this
   has to be static-only. Build exactly what it describes; it's already been through a full design
   review and every technical claim in it was independently verified against PGPatcher's own real
   source, so treat it as ground truth, not a rough draft.
2. `vortex-tools/vortex-collection-tools/design/mockup-pgpatcher-priority-merge-tool.html` -- the
   director-approved visual mockup. Match its visual language closely: same dark palette/CSS custom
   properties, same class names where they already exist (`.bucket`, `.bucket--review`,
   `.reconcile-row`, `.pgp-panels`/`.pgp-panel`/`.pgp-row` etc.) -- this mockup went through two
   real rounds of director feedback (the four-bucket match report, then a correction to make the sort
   screen match the real Load Order Editor's panel pair exactly), so its shape is settled, not a
   starting suggestion.

--- WHAT TO BUILD ---

**Tech: plain HTML/CSS/JS, one page, no framework, no build step, no npm dependencies.** This is a
hard requirement from the spec (the whole point is "the only tool the end-user has is a browser"),
not a preference. `FileReader`/`JSON.parse` to read the two uploaded files, a plain JS module for
the matching engine, native HTML5 drag-and-drop for the sort screen, a client-side `Blob` + download
link for the final file. Nothing is ever sent to any server.

1. **Matching engine** (spec's own "Matching algorithm" section) as a self-contained JS module,
   dependency-free so it's easy to unit-reason-about even without a test framework:
   - Tier 1: exact string match, auto-applied.
   - Tier 2: normalized match (spec gives the exact regex:
     `/\s+[\d.]+(?:\s+[\d.]+)*\s*$/` stripped from the end, then case-insensitive compare),
     auto-applied but flagged in the report as "matched via normalization."
   - Tier 3: fuzzy candidates against the REMAINING unmatched author entries only, human-confirmed,
     never auto-applied. Exact similarity algorithm is your call (longest-common-prefix, a basic
     edit-distance ratio, whatever's simplest to get right) -- **bias the "worth showing" threshold
     loose, not tight**: every fuzzy candidate already requires human confirmation before anything
     happens, so showing an extra low-quality candidate costs a moment of the user's attention while
     hiding a real match costs them noticing it's silently missing. Show multiple candidates per
     unmatched mod when more than one clears the floor (mockup's own "2 other candidates" link).
   - Tier 4: no match at all -- stays exactly as-is in the end-user's file, no action, shown as a
     count-only bucket.
   - **Canonical-name rule**: on any match (any tier), the OUTPUT key is always the end-user's own
     name string, never the author's -- only `priority` travels from the author's entry. Author-only
     entries (present in the author's file, no match in the end-user's file at all) are dropped
     entirely, never carried into the output as new keys.
   - **Merge scope**: only `priority` is overwritten. `enabled` and `meshesignored` always stay
     whatever the end-user's own file already had.

2. **Upload screen** -- two drop targets (author's file / your file), drag-and-drop or click-to-
   browse, real client-side `FileReader`/`JSON.parse` (handle a malformed/non-JSON file with a
   plain error message, not a silent failure or a raw exception in the console). Privacy note stays
   visible per the mockup ("nothing leaves your browser").

3. **Match report** -- the four-bucket layout from the mockup, same visual weighting (exact + reads
   collapsed/low-key, normalized flagged but still low-key, "Needs your review" gets real visual
   weight -- larger, warm-colored, not buried, per `docs/UX-UI-DEPENDENCY-DESIGNER.md`'s confidence-
   tier guidance the mockup was built against). Exact and normalized buckets expand to a scrollable
   list on click (mockup's own `▾ show list` affordance -- make it real, not decorative).

4. **Reconciliation step** -- one row per Tier-3 unmatched mod, its best candidate(s), **Confirm
   match** / **Not the same mod** actions per row (mockup's own `.reconcile-row` shape). Nothing
   proceeds to the sort screen with an unconfirmed fuzzy match still pending -- either force
   resolution of every row first, or make it clear unresolved rows just won't get a priority (match
   the spec's own "never auto-apply" rule either way, use judgment on which UX is less annoying, flag
   the choice in the handoff).

5. **Sort screen -- real, working two-panel drag-and-drop, not the simplified mockup-only markup.**
   The mockup's own section 4 shows the TARGET visual shape (ranked panel + "New mods" panel side by
   side, full per-panel toolbar: search/Sort A-Z/Priority order [ranked panel only]/Select all/Invert
   selection/Clear selection/selection count, per-row enabled checkbox, drag handle) but its JS is
   non-functional (a static screenshot-equivalent). For the REAL interaction behavior, read
   `web/public/pgpatcher-app.js` lines ~470-535 (drag start/dragover/drop, shift-click range-select,
   ctrl/cmd-click toggle-select, `pgpToggleEnabled` around line 100) -- this is the first drag-and-
   drop list this whole project built and it already solved the exact interaction model you need
   (search doesn't hide non-matching rows, it highlights matches -- keep that behavior too). Port the
   INTERACTION MODEL, not the code verbatim -- that file talks to a real backend (save/build API
   calls) ModruleSync doesn't have; you're reimplementing the same drag/select/sort/search UX in a
   plain client-side array with no server round-trip. `priority = order.length - index` is the same
   real computation the existing `/save` route already uses (spec's own explicit callout) -- reuse
   that formula, don't invent a different one.
   - Ranked panel starts pre-filled: matched mods carry the author's priority (rank order = sorted by
     that priority, highest first, same as `compareMods`' real descending sort spec cites), tagged
     "from author"; anything the user drags/reorders after that gets tagged "hand-adjusted" (mockup's
     own two tag states).
   - "New mods" panel holds every Tier-4 (no-match) mod -- dragging one into the ranked panel gives it
     a real priority the same way the real tool's own unranked→ranked drag already works.

6. **Download** -- a client-side `Blob`("application/json") + a real download link/button, filename
   `modrules.json`, no server round-trip. The merged JSON's actual shape must match what PGPatcher's
   own `PGModManager::loadJSON` expects (`priority`, `enabled`, `meshesignored` per mod key --
   check `skyrim-modding/pgpatcher-fork/PGLib/src/PGModManager.cpp` around line 200-230, already read
   once for the spec review, if you need the exact field shape) so a real PGPatcher can load the
   output file without modification.

--- VERIFY ---

There's no existing test framework in this new repo and no backend to hit -- verification here means:
1. Build two small SYNTHETIC `modrules.json` fixtures by hand (a handful of mods each, deliberately
   covering: an exact-match pair, a version-suffix pair that should hit Tier 2, a pair close enough to
   need Tier 3 confirmation, an author-only entry that should be dropped, an end-user-only entry that
   should land in "New mods"). Load the real page in a browser yourself and walk the full flow against
   these fixtures end to end -- confirm each bucket gets the right count, confirm the canonical-name
   rule holds (check the OUTPUT file's keys are the end-user's names, not the author's), confirm the
   downloaded file's shape is valid JSON PGPatcher could actually load.
2. This is real UI/interaction work (drag-and-drop, multi-select, live search) -- CAN'T be verified by
   a syntax check alone. Actually load and click through it. Say plainly in the handoff which parts
   you exercised live vs. which you're confident about from code-reading alone.
3. `node -c` (or equivalent) on every JS file regardless, as a baseline.

--- COMMIT ---

Inside `F:\Claude Workspace\skyrim-modding\modrule-sync` (its own repo, its own remote) -- narrow
`git add`, commit, and push to `origin main`. Do NOT enable GitHub Pages yourself -- flag it in the
handoff once the build is real and verified; the design side will turn Pages on once it's confirmed
working, not before.

Write a handoff to this repo's own `prompts/handoff-latest.md` (create the file -- this is its
first one) per this workspace's own standing rule -- include what you built, what you verified live
vs. by reading, any judgment calls (similarity algorithm choice, reconciliation-gating choice), and
flag the Pages activation as the next step.
